Provider records DO expire: reprovide.validity is honoured and providerRecordPolicy already sets it to one hour. Only providers.provideValidity/cleanupInterval are ignored. Four wrong answers on this already exist

Runaway Durable Object cost: the $34,895 figure is ONE self-report on Hacker News (thewillmoss, 2026-04-16, 31 points) — the bill was for ~930bn row reads/day, not alarm invocations, and the cause included 60+ preview deployments. What is independently corroborated is that Cloudflare has NO spending limits. setAlarm overrides rather than stacks; a throwing alarm() handler retries 6 times with backoff.

Cloudflare spend: budget alerts exist since 2026-04-13 and are default-on since 2026-07-20 at $10, but Cloudflare's own docs say they are informational and DO NOT cap usage. Two hard rules for this project: (1) no preview deployments of the hosted tier — 60+ previews were the multiplier in the cited incident, not the alarm; (2) the set of idFromName() names must be closed and short (bootstrap-us/-eu/-sam — South America, not APAC; the owner named the three on 2026-08-25) — a name derived from visitor-controlled input lets a public cohort create unbounded objects, each with storage and an alarm.

Durable Object siting, read from Cloudflare's data-location docs 2026-08-25: locationHint is best-effort and NOT a guarantee, so never claim where an object runs; jurisdiction IS binding but takes only eu/us/fedramp, so the EU object should be created in the eu jurisdiction while South America can only ever be a hint (sam); and location is fixed by an object's very FIRST get() and never changes afterwards — so exactly one call site may create these objects, or a stray get() sites them permanently in the wrong place.
